title: Object detection for autonomous driving (illustrative demo)

paper.name: Illustrative paper: ML object detection for autonomous driving
paper.one_line: A detector trained on a daytime clear-weather driving dataset reports strong mAP, but is not evaluated in rain, fog, or low light.

established.research_question: Can a convolutional detector localize and classify common traffic objects well enough for an autonomous-driving perception stack on a standard daytime benchmark?
established.methodology: Supervised training of a one-stage detector on labeled camera frames; evaluation with mean average precision (mAP) and per-class AP on a held-out clear-weather split.
findings: Overall mAP on the clear daytime test split is competitive with contemporaneous baselines reported in the paper.
Per-class AP is strongest for cars and pedestrians; weaker for rare classes (e.g. bicycles at distance).
Inference latency on the authors' reference GPU meets their stated real-time threshold for the demo vehicle setup.
limitations: Training and test data are dominated by daytime, clear-weather scenes.
No systematic evaluation in rain, fog, snow, or low-light / night driving.
Dataset geography and sensor suite are fixed; cross-city and cross-camera generalization are not measured.
The paper does not report closed-loop driving outcomes — perception metrics only.
conclusions: Within the clear daytime setting, the method is presented as a viable perception component.
Authors note that robustness to adverse conditions remains open.

gap_assessment.summary: Yes — the paper itself leaves adverse-weather and low-light robustness largely untested, while claiming utility for autonomous driving where those conditions matter.

gaps.title: Adverse weather and low-light robustness not evaluated
support_passages: Limitation: no systematic evaluation in rain, fog, snow, or low-light / night driving.
Authors note that robustness to adverse conditions remains open.
gaps.why_it_matters: Autonomous driving must operate outside clear daytime. Without those tests, the paper's practical claim is incomplete.
gaps.what_it_could_establish: Whether detection quality holds (or fails) under rain, fog, and night, and by how much mAP drops.

gaps.title: Cross-city / cross-sensor generalization unmeasured
support_passages: Dataset geography and sensor suite are fixed; cross-city and cross-camera generalization are not measured.
gaps.why_it_matters: A single geography and camera stack can overstate readiness for deployment elsewhere.
gaps.what_it_could_establish: How much performance transfers when city or camera changes, without claiming field-wide novelty.

author_future_work.text: Evaluate the detector under adverse weather and nighttime conditions.
author_future_work.practical_meaning: Collect or license rain/fog/night frames (or use a public adverse-weather driving set), re-run the same mAP protocol, and report degradation vs the clear daytime baseline.

author_future_work.text: Explore domain adaptation or augmentation for robustness.
author_future_work.practical_meaning: Try weather augmentations or adaptation methods and compare to the unaugmented model on the same adverse split.

next_steps.title: Adverse-condition evaluation suite
involves: Define rain, fog, and low-light evaluation splits (public sets or newly labeled frames).
Freeze the trained weights from the paper setting; measure mAP and per-class AP per condition.
Report absolute scores and drop vs clear daytime.
next_steps.would_help_establish: How far the published clear-weather result extends into conditions the authors already flag as open.
suggested_experiments: Failure-case gallery (missed pedestrians at night, false positives in spray)
Optional: confidence calibration under each condition

next_steps.title: Targeted data collection or augmentation for the weakest condition
involves: Pick the condition with the largest drop from step 1.
Add labeled data or physics-inspired augmentations for that condition.
Retrain or fine-tune and re-evaluate on the held-out adverse split.
next_steps.would_help_establish: Whether the limitation is mainly data coverage vs a harder algorithmic failure mode.
suggested_experiments: Same test protocol as the paper plus the new adverse split

next_steps.title: Cross-dataset check (different city or camera)
involves: Run the released model (or a faithful reimplementation) on another public driving detection set.
Compare per-class AP shifts without changing training.
next_steps.would_help_establish: Sensitivity to geography/sensor — an inferred gap from the paper's fixed setup, not a claim that nobody has studied this.
suggested_experiments: Error analysis by object size and lighting
next_steps.literature_note: To argue this is still open in the field, you would need related work on domain generalization for driving detectors — not available from this paper alone.

no_gap_alternative.when_to_use: If a paper already closes the obvious limitations and states no open future work.
suggestions: Replicate on a newer public benchmark the authors did not use.
Compare against a stronger contemporary baseline.
Follow an explicitly stated future direction only — do not invent a gap.

from_uploaded_paper: All findings, limitations, and author future-work items above are grounded in the demo pack's paper-style claims.
Gap g1 is treated as author-acknowledged because the paper states adverse conditions remain open.
would_need_related_literature: Whether adverse-weather detection is still a novel gap across the whole field.
Whether a specific newer architecture already solves the limitation.
Priority 3's novelty as a research contribution beyond this paper's setup.

definitions.TAM: Total Addressable Market — everyone who could buy in the broad category (e.g. global ADAS / autonomous perception software spend).
definitions.SAM: Serviceable Available Market — the slice you can serve with your offer (e.g. camera-based detection for passenger ADAS in regions you can sell into).
definitions.SOM: Serviceable Obtainable Market — what you can realistically win in a near horizon (capacity, sales, competition).

how_calculated: Top-down: start from an industry TAM figure → apply filters (region, segment, product type) to get SAM → apply expected share or capacity to get SOM.
Bottom-up: (# target vehicles or fleets) × (attach rate) × (ASP or subscription) = SAM or SOM building blocks.
Consistency rule: SOM ≤ SAM ≤ TAM (same currency, same year).
